voix_intro: Vrai ou faux ? Quatre idées reçues sur l'histoire. Compte tes bonnes réponses !

idees.affirmation: « Les Vikings portaient des casques à cornes. »

panneaux.texte: Aucun casque viking à cornes n'a été retrouvé.
panneaux.sous_texte: Le seul casque viking complet n'en a pas.

panneaux.texte: Une tapisserie d'époque montre bien des cornes…
panneaux.sous_texte: … sans doute pas portées au combat.
panneaux.voix: Une tapisserie d'époque montre bien des cornes, sans doute pas portées au combat.

panneaux.texte: Un opéra de Wagner l'a popularisée en 1876.
panneaux.voix: Un opéra de Wagner l'a popularisée en 1876.

sources.titre: Did Vikings really wear horned helmets?
sources.extrait: And despite years of searching, archaeologists have yet to uncover a Viking-era helmet embellished with horns. […] the 10th-century artifact has a rounded iron cap, a guard around the eyes and nose, and no horns to speak of.

sources.titre: Iconic Viking Horned Helmets Are Actually 3,000 Years Old
sources.extrait: Viking society only developed in the 9th century C.E., and there is no sign that Vikings really wore horned helmets.

sources.titre: Horned 'Viking' helmets were actually from a different civilization, archaeologists say
sources.extrait: […] Vikings wore bulls' horns on their helmets, although there is no evidence they ever did.

sources.titre: Did Vikings Actually Have Horns on Their Helmets?
sources.extrait: It is likely that Vikings did not wear horns on their helmets, particularly for battle and non-ceremonial purposes. […] There is only one preserved helmet from the Viking Age and this does not have horns. […] a tapestry was found on which horned helmets are also depicted. […] The image of Vikings with horned helmets first gained popularity in 1876 […] costume designer Carl Emil Doepler included them in the costumes for Wagner's opera

idees.affirmation: « Des mammouths vivaient encore quand on a bâti les pyramides de Gizeh. »

panneaux.voix: Les pyramides ont environ 4 500 ans, les derniers mammouths 4 000.

panneaux.texte: Sur l'île Wrangel, au large de la Sibérie.

sources.titre: New genetic study reveals the woolly mammoths' journey towards extinction
sources.extrait: What eventually caused the extinction of the Wrangel population some 4,000 years ago remains a mystery.

sources.titre: The last woolly mammoths offer new clues to why this species died out
sources.extrait: Four thousand years ago, the world's last woolly mammoth took its final breath. […] The last of this species lived on Wrangel Island. That's off the coast of what is now Siberia.
The monumental tombs are relics of Egypt's Old Kingdom era and were constructed some 4,500 years ago.

panneaux.voix: Napoléon mesurait environ un mètre soixante-huit : dans la moyenne de l'époque.

panneaux.texte: Des caricatures anglaises, qui le dessinaient minuscule.

sources.extrait: Sources consequently estimate that Napoleon was probably closer to 5'6" or 5'7" (1.68 or 1.7 meters) than to 5'2". […] most Frenchmen stood between 5'2" and 5'6" (1.58 and 1.68 meters) tall […] Napoleon was thus average or taller, no matter the interpretation.
la taille de Napoléon n'était pas inférieure à 1m.686

sources.titre: Why Do We Think Napoleon Was Short?
sources.extrait: In fact, he was probably of average height. […] that equals around 1.67 meters, or just under 5'6" […] which is a little above average for a French man in the early 1800s. […] Gillray's cartoon depicts a tiny Napoleon wearing boots that dwarf him, tearing his hair out in rage. […] The name "Little Boney" would stick

idees.affirmation: « La tour Eiffel devait être démontée après 20 ans. »

panneaux.texte: Gustave Eiffel n'avait un permis que pour 20 ans.
panneaux.sous_texte: Ensuite, la Ville pouvait la démolir.
panneaux.voix: Son permis ne durait que 20 ans. Ensuite, la Ville pouvait la démolir.

panneaux.texte: Antenne géante : 70 ans de plus dès 1910.
panneaux.voix: Devenue antenne géante, elle obtient 70 ans de plus.

sources.titre: Why was the Eiffel Tower kept?
sources.extrait: The Eiffel Tower was supposed to be dismantled after 20 years. […] In 1910, the Eiffel Tower could have been demolished! […] Gustave Eiffel had only been given a 20-year permit to use the land. […] But its use as a giant radio antenna saved it from destruction! […] Gustave Eiffel was granted an extension to his concession for another 70 years, starting on 1st January 1910.

sources.titre: How science saved the Eiffel Tower
sources.extrait: Eiffel's four-legged iron archway was supposed to last only 20 years. […] the city could choose to tear it down […] it was another area of research — radio — that ensured Eiffel's Tower would not be torn down. […] In 1910, the city of Paris renewed the structure's permit for another 70 years.
